celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ Exalted is ﴿الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ the Quran, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood ﴿عَلَى عَبْدِهِ﴾ Muhammad ﴿لِيَكُونَ لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ i.e. humans and jinn, not the angels ﴿نَذِيرًا﴾ one who warns of the punishment of Allah.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ whose nature it is to be created ﴿فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا﴾ He fashioned it in due proportion.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ Allah, i.e. other than Him ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ these are the idols ﴿لَا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئًا وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ وَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ ضَرًّا﴾ i.e. to ward it off ﴿وَلَا نَفْعًا﴾ i.e. to bring it ﴿وَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ مَوْتًا وَلَا حَيَاةً﴾ i.e. causing anyone to die or giving anyone life ﴿وَلَا نُشُورًا﴾ raising the dead.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هَذَا﴾ i.e. the Quran is not ﴿إِلَّا إِفْكٌ﴾ a lie ﴿افْتَرَاهُ﴾ Muhammad ﴿وَأَعَانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ﴾ and they are of the People of the Book. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَقَدْ جَاءُو ظُلْمًا وَزُورًا﴾ disbelief and lying, i.e. with them.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ also: it is ﴿أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ their lies — plural of أُسْطُورَة, with ḍamma ﴿اكْتَتَبَهَا﴾ he had them copied from those people by someone else ﴿فَهِيَ تُمْلَى﴾ are read ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ so that he memorises them ﴿بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾ morning and evening. Allah the Exalted said, refuting them:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿قُلْ أَنْزَلَهُ الَّذِي يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ﴾ the unseen ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفُورًا﴾ to the believers ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to them.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا مَالِ هَذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ لَوْلَا﴾ why not ﴿أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيرًا﴾ confirming him.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَوْ يُلْقَى إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ﴾ from the sky, which he could spend and not need to walk in the markets seeking a livelihood ﴿أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ an orchard ﴿يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا﴾ i.e. from its fruits, and be content with it; in one reading [نَأْكُلُ] with nūn, i.e. we, so that he would have a distinction over us by it ﴿وَقَالَ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, to the believers ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا﴾ deceived, overpowered in his mind. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ [calling you] bewitched, in need of something to spend and of an angel to stand with him in the matter ﴿فَضَلُّوا﴾ thereby, from guidance ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to it.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ abundant is the good of ﴿الَّذِي إِنْ شَاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْرًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ﴾ which they said, of the treasure and the orchard ﴿جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ﴾ in this world — because He has willed to give them to him in the Hereafter ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ﴾ in the jussive (majzūm) ﴿لَكَ قُصُورًا﴾ as well; and in one reading in the nominative, as a resumption (istiʾnāf).

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالسَّاعَةِ﴾ the Resurrection ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِمَنْ كَذَّبَ بِالسَّاعَةِ سَعِيرًا﴾ a kindled fire, i.e. intensified.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِذَا رَأَتْهُمْ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ سَمِعُوا لَهَا تَغَيُّظًا﴾ a boiling, like an angry man when his breast boils with anger ﴿وَزَفِيرًا﴾ an intense sound; or [the meaning of] hearing the raging is seeing it and knowing it.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَإِذَا أُلْقُوا مِنْهَا مَكَانًا ضَيِّقًا﴾ with doubling and without doubling, in that it is made narrow upon them; and مِنْهَا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَكَانًا, because originally it is an adjective (ṣifa) of it ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ﴾ shackled, their hands having been joined, i.e. brought together, to their necks in the iron collars; and the doubling is for intensification ﴿دَعَوْا هُنَالِكَ ثُبُورًا﴾ destruction. And it is said to them:

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿لَا تَدْعُوا الْيَوْمَ ثُبُورًا وَاحِدًا وَادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾ like your punishment.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿قُلْ أَذَلِكَ﴾ which is mentioned, of the threat and the description of the Fire ﴿خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ الْخُلْدِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ﴾ it ﴿الْمُتَّقُونَ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ﴾ in His knowledge, the Exalted ﴿جَزَاءً﴾ a reward ﴿وَمَصِيرًا﴾ a place of return.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا مَا يَشَاءُونَ خَالِدِينَ﴾ a permanent ḥāl (ḥāl lāzima, circumstantial) ﴿كَانَ﴾ the promise to them of what was mentioned ﴿عَلَى رَبِّكَ وَعْدًا مَسْئُولًا﴾ asked for by those to whom it was promised: {رَبَّنَا وَآتِنَا مَا وَعَدْتَنَا عَلَى رُسُلِكَ}, or the angels ask for it on their behalf: {رَبَّنَا وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدْتَهُمْ}.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾ with nūn and with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] ﴿وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, of the angels, ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the jinn ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾ the Exalted — with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and with nūn — to the worshipped, to establish the proof against the worshippers ﴿أَأَنْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, with the second changed into an alif, with it softened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other, or without it ﴿أَضْلَلْتُمْ عِبَادِي هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ did you make them fall into error by commanding them to worship you ﴿أَمْ هُمْ ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ﴾ the path of truth, by themselves?

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ﴾ declaring You free of what does not befit You ﴿مَا كَانَ يَنْبَغِي﴾ it was not right ﴿لَنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ﴾ i.e. other than You ﴿مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ the first mafʿūl (object), and مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation, and what precedes it is the second; so how could we command [them] to worship us? ﴿وَلَكِنْ مَتَّعْتَهُمْ وَآبَاءَهُمْ﴾ before them, with long life and ample provision ﴿حَتَّى نَسُوا الذِّكْرَ﴾ they abandoned the admonition and faith in the Quran ﴿وَكَانُوا قَوْمًا بُورًا﴾ ruined. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ﴾ the worshipped have given the lie to the worshippers ﴿بِمَا تَقُولُونَ﴾ with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ]: that they are gods ﴿فَمَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ with the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] and the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] [تَسْتَطِيعُونَ], i.e. neither they nor you ﴿صَرْفًا﴾ warding off the punishment from you ﴿وَلَا نَصْرًا﴾ protecting you from it ﴿وَمَنْ يَظْلِمْ﴾ associates partners [with Allah] ﴿مِنْكُمْ نُذِقْهُ عَذَابًا كَبِيرًا﴾ severe, in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشُونَ فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ﴾ so you are like them in that, and what was said to you was said to them ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً﴾ a trial: the rich is tried by the poor, the healthy by the sick, and the noble by the lowly; the second in each case says, «Why am I not like the first?» — in each case ﴿أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾ with what you hear from those by whom you are tried — a question (istifhām) in the sense of a command, i.e. be patient ﴿وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيرًا﴾ of who is patient and who is impatient.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَاءَنَا﴾ do not fear the resurrection ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why not ﴿أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ and been messengers to us ﴿أَوْ نَرَى رَبَّنَا﴾ and He would tell [us] that Muhammad is His Messenger. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿لَقَدِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ they have become arrogant ﴿فِي﴾ the matter of ﴿أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَعَتَوْا﴾ transgressed ﴿عُتُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ by asking to see Allah the Exalted in this world; and عُتُوًّا is with wāw according to its original form, unlike عِتِيًّا, with substitution [of yāʾ], in [Sura] Maryam.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ﴾ among all creatures — it is the Day of Resurrection; and its accusative is by an implied اذْكُرْ (remember) ﴿لَا بُشْرَى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers, unlike the believers, for they have the good news of Paradise ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا﴾ as was their custom in this world when hardship befell them, i.e. «a refuge, a refuge sought!» — they seek refuge from the angels. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَقَدِمْنَا﴾ We turned ﴿إِلَى مَا عَمِلُوا مِنْ عَمَلٍ﴾ of good, such as charity, maintaining ties of kinship, hosting a guest and helping one in distress, in this world ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ هَبَاءً مَنْثُورًا﴾ it is what is seen in the openings upon which the sun falls, like scattered dust; i.e. like it in being of no benefit, since there is no reward in it because its condition [faith] is absent; and they are recompensed for it in this world.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا﴾ than the disbelievers in this world ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا﴾ than them, i.e. a place of the midday rest (qāʾila) in it, which is resting at midday in the heat; and from that it has been deduced that the reckoning is completed in half a day, as has come in the hadith.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّمَاءُ﴾ every heaven ﴿بِالْغَمَامِ﴾ with it, and it is white cloud ﴿وَنُزِّلَ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ from every heaven ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾ It is the Day of Resurrection, and its accusative is by an implied اذْكُرْ (remember). In one reading with doubling of the shīn of تَشَقَّقُ, by assimilating into it the second tāʾ of the original; and in another [نُنْزِلُ] with two nūns, the second with sukūn, with ḍamma on the lām and the accusative of الْمَلَائِكَة.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ no one shares it with Him ﴿وَكَانَ﴾ the day ﴿يَوْمًا عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ عَسِيرًا﴾ unlike the believers.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ﴾ the polytheist ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, who had uttered the two testimonies of faith and then went back on it to please Ubayy ibn Khalaf ﴿عَلَى يَدَيْهِ﴾ out of remorse and regret, on the Day of Resurrection ﴿يَقُولُ يَا﴾ for calling attention (tanbīh) ﴿لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ﴾ Muhammad ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ a path to guidance.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَا وَيْلَتَى﴾ its alif is a substitute for the yāʾ of the possessive, i.e. وَيْلَتِي, and its meaning is «my ruin» ﴿لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلَانًا﴾ i.e. Ubayy ﴿خَلِيلًا﴾

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿لَقَدْ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ الذِّكْرِ﴾ the Quran ﴿بَعْدَ إِذْ جَاءَنِي﴾ by turning me back from believing in it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِلْإِنْسَانِ﴾ the disbeliever ﴿خَذُولًا﴾ in that he abandons him and disowns him in time of affliction.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الرَّسُولُ﴾ Muhammad ﴿يَا رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي﴾ Quraysh ﴿اتَّخَذُوا هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا﴾ abandoned. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We have made for you an enemy among the polytheists of your people ﴿جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ﴾ before you ﴿عَدُوًّا مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ the polytheists; so be patient as they were patient ﴿وَكَفَى بِرَبِّكَ هَادِيًا﴾ for you ﴿وَنَصِيرًا﴾ a helper for you against your enemies.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا﴾ why not ﴿نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms? Allah the Exalted said: We have sent it down ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. in parts ﴿لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ﴾ to strengthen your heart ﴿وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا﴾ We brought it little by little, slowly and deliberately, so that understanding and memorising it would be easy.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَلَا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ﴾ to invalidate your cause ﴿إِلَّا جِئْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ that repels it ﴿وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا﴾ as an explanation for them.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ i.e. are driven ﴿إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا﴾ that is Hell ﴿وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا﴾ more mistaken in way than others, and that is their disbelief.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Torah ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيرًا﴾ a helper.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَقُلْنَا اذْهَبَا إِلَى الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. the Copts, Pharaoh and his people; so they went to them with the message, and they denied them ﴿فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ تَدْمِيرًا﴾ We destroyed them utterly.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿قَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمَّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ﴾ by denying Nūḥ, because of his long stay among them, so that he is as though [many] messengers; or because denying him is denying the rest of the messengers, since they share in bringing the message of Allah's oneness ﴿أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ the answer of لَمَّا ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ after them ﴿آيَةً﴾ a lesson ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful, besides what befalls them in this world.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿عَادًا﴾ the people of Hūd ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾ the people of Ṣāliḥ ﴿وَأَصْحَابَ الرَّسِّ﴾ the name of a well; their prophet is said to have been Shuʿayb, and it is said someone else. They were sitting around it, and it collapsed with them and their dwellings ﴿وَقُرُونًا﴾ peoples ﴿بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ i.e. between ʿĀd and the People of the Well.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ in establishing the proof against them, so We did not destroy them except after warning ﴿وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيرًا﴾ We destroyed utterly, for their denial of their prophets.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers of Mecca passed ﴿عَلَى الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ﴾ maṣdar (verbal noun) of سَاءَ — with stones; and it is the greatest of the towns of the people of Lūṭ, and Allah destroyed its people for their committing the abomination ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَهَا﴾ on their journeys to Syria, and take heed? The question (istifhām) is for making them affirm (taqrīr) ﴿بَلْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ﴾ fear ﴿نُشُورًا﴾ resurrection, so they do not believe.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَوْكَ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ an object of mockery, saying ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا﴾ in his claim — belittling him as unworthy of the message.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy [إِنَّ], and its noun (ism) is omitted, i.e. إِنَّهُ ﴿كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا﴾ to turn us away ﴿عَنْ آلِهَتِنَا لَوْلَا أَنْ صَبَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا﴾ we would have been turned away from them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ﴾ with their own eyes, in the Hereafter ﴿مَنْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا﴾ more mistaken in way — they or the believers.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ tell me ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾ i.e. what he desires; the second mafʿūl (object) is placed first because it is more important; and the clause مَنِ اتَّخَذَ is the first mafʿūl of رَأَيْتُ [Translator's note: as printed; the verb in the ayah is رَأَيْتَ], and the second is ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ a guardian who guards him from following his desire? No.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ a hearing of understanding ﴿أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ what you say to them ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا﴾ more mistaken in way than them, because they [the cattle] submit to whoever takes care of them, while these do not obey their Master who bestows favours on them.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ look ﴿إِلَى﴾ the doing of ﴿رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ﴾ from the time of daybreak to the time of sunrise ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ﴾ your Lord ﴿لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِنًا﴾ fixed, not disappearing with the rising of the sun ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا الشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. the shadow ﴿دَلِيلًا﴾ for were it not for the sun, the shadow would not be known.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. the extended shadow ﴿إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا﴾ imperceptibly, with the rising of the sun.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا﴾ a covering like clothing ﴿وَالنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا﴾ rest for the bodies by the cessation of work ﴿وَجَعَلَ النَّهَارَ نُشُورًا﴾ in which one spreads out to seek provision and other things.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّيَاحَ﴾ and in one reading [الرِّيحَ] ﴿نُشُرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ dispersed, ahead of the rain; in one reading with sukūn on the shīn, for lightening; in another with sukūn on it and fatḥa on the nūn, as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and in another [بُشْرًا] with sukūn on it and ḍamma on the one-dotted letter [bāʾ] in place of the nūn, i.e. bearing good tidings. The singular of the first is نَشُور, like رَسُول, and of the last بَشِير ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً طَهُورًا﴾ purifying.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا﴾ with the yāʾ undoubled; masculine and feminine are the same in it — He made it masculine with regard to [the sense of] «place» ﴿وَنُسْقِيَهُ﴾ i.e. the water ﴿مِمَّا خَلَقْنَا أَنْعَامًا﴾ camels, cattle and sheep ﴿وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرًا﴾ plural of إِنْسَان; its original form is أَنَاسِين, then the nūn was changed into a yāʾ and the [other] yāʾ was assimilated into it; or it is the plural of إِنْسِيّ.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. the water ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾ its original form is يَتَذَكَّرُوا; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl; and in one reading [لِيَذْكُرُوا] with sukūn on the dhāl and ḍamma on the kāf — i.e. [to remember] the favour of Allah through it ﴿فَأَبَى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا﴾ ingratitude for the favour, in that they said, «We were given rain by such-and-such a star.»

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَذِيرًا﴾ to warn its people; but We have sent you to the people of all the towns as a warner, so that your reward may be great.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿فَلَا تُطِعِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in their desires ﴿وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿جِهَادًا كَبِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ sent them forth side by side ﴿هَذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ﴾ intensely sweet ﴿وَهَذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ﴾ intensely salty ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا﴾ a barrier, so that neither mixes with the other ﴿وَحِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا﴾ i.e. a screen by which their mixing is prevented.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ بَشَرًا﴾ from sperm, a human being ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَبًا﴾ having lineage ﴿وَصِهْرًا﴾ having in-laws, in that he marries, whether male or female, seeking offspring ﴿وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ able to do what He wills.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ by worshipping it ﴿وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ﴾ by abandoning it, and that is the idols ﴿وَكَانَ الْكَافِرُ عَلَى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيرًا﴾ a helper of Satan, by obeying him.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا﴾ of Paradise ﴿وَنَذِيرًا﴾ warning of the Fire.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿قُلْ مَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ i.e. for conveying what I have been sent with ﴿مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿مَنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا﴾ a path, by spending his wealth in what pleases Him, the Exalted — I do not prevent him from that.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ﴾ accompanied ﴿بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ i.e. say: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah ﴿وَكَفَى بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾ knowing; بِذُنُوبٍ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it [خَبِيرًا]; [the one sufficing is] He.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ of the days of this world, i.e. their measure, because there was no sun then; and had He willed, He would have created them in a moment, and turning away from that is to teach His creation deliberateness ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ in the language it is the throne of kingship ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the pronoun of اسْتَوَى, i.e. a rising that befits Him ﴿فَاسْأَلْ﴾ O man ﴿بِهِ﴾ about the All-Merciful ﴿خَبِيرًا﴾ who will inform you of His attributes.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ﴾ to the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ قَالُوا وَمَا الرَّحْمَنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا﴾ with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] and the lower-dotted letter [yāʾ] — and the one commanding is Muhammad — when we do not know Him? No ﴿وَزَادَهُمْ﴾ this saying to them ﴿نُفُورًا﴾ from faith. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ Majestic is ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا﴾ twelve: Aries (al-ḥamal), Taurus (al-thawr), Gemini (al-jawzāʾ), Cancer (al-saraṭān), Leo (al-asad), Virgo (al-sunbula), Libra (al-mīzān), Scorpio (al-ʿaqrab), Sagittarius (al-qaws), Capricorn (al-jady), Aquarius (al-dalw) and Pisces (al-ḥūt). They are the mansions of the seven moving planets: Mars, which has Aries and Scorpio; Venus, which has Taurus and Libra; Mercury, which has Gemini and Virgo; the Moon, which has Cancer; the Sun, which has Leo; Jupiter, which has Sagittarius and Pisces; and Saturn, which has Capricorn and Aquarius ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا﴾ also ﴿سِرَاجًا﴾ that is the sun ﴿وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا﴾ and in one reading [سُرُجًا] in the plural, i.e. luminaries; and He singled out the moon among them for mention because of a kind of excellence it has.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً﴾ i.e. each of them succeeds the other ﴿لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ﴾ with doubling and without doubling, as has preceded — [to remember] what good he missed in one of them, and do it in the other ﴿أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُورًا﴾ gratitude for his Lord's favour to him in them.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it are adjectives (ṣifāt) of it up to أُولَئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ, apart from what is parenthetical within it ﴿الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾ i.e. with calm and humility ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ﴾ with what they dislike ﴿قَالُوا سَلَامًا﴾ i.e. words in which they are safe from sin.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا﴾ plural of سَاجِد ﴿وَقِيَامًا﴾ in the sense of «standing», praying at night.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا﴾ inseparable.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ﴾ evil is ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ it [Hell], i.e. as a place of settling and staying.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا﴾ on their dependants ﴿لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma on its first letter, i.e. are not stingy ﴿وَكَانَ﴾ their spending ﴿بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ extravagance and stinginess ﴿قَوَامًا﴾ moderate.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ the killing of ﴿إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ any one of the three ﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾ a punishment.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿يُضَاعَفْ﴾ and in one reading [يُضَعَّفْ] with doubling ﴿لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ﴾ with both verbs in the jussive (majzūm) as a badal (substitute), and with both in the nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf) ﴿مُهَانًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial).

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ among them ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ﴾ mentioned ﴿حَسَنَاتٍ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ i.e. He has always been characterised by that.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَمَنْ تَابَ﴾ from his sins, other than those mentioned ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَابًا﴾ i.e. he returns to Him truly, and He recompenses him with good.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾ i.e. lies and falsehood ﴿وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ of ugly speech and other things ﴿مَرُّوا كِرَامًا﴾ turning away from it.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا﴾ are admonished ﴿بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿لَمْ يَخِرُّوا﴾ fall ﴿عَلَيْهَا صُمًّا وَعُمْيَانًا﴾ rather they fall down hearing, seeing and benefiting.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا﴾ in the plural and in the singular ﴿قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ﴾ for us, by our seeing them obedient to You ﴿وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا﴾ in goodness.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الْغُرْفَةَ﴾ the highest rank in Paradise ﴿بِمَا صَبَرُوا﴾ in obeying Allah ﴿وَيُلَقَّوْنَ﴾ with doubling, and without doubling with fatḥa on the yāʾ ﴿فِيهَا﴾ in the lofty chamber ﴿تَحِيَّةً وَسَلَامًا﴾ from the angels.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ a place of staying for them. And أُولَئِكَ and what follows it is the khabar (predicate) of عِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ, the mubtadaʾ (subject).

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muhammad, to the people of Mecca ﴿مَا﴾ negating (nāfiya) ﴿يَعْبَأُ﴾ cares ﴿بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلَا دُعَاؤُكُمْ﴾ to Him in hardships, so that He removes them ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ i.e. so how would He care for you, when ﴿كَذَّبْتُمْ﴾ the Messenger and the Quran ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ﴾ the punishment ﴿لِزَامًا﴾ cleaving to you in the Hereafter, after what befalls you in this world; and seventy of them were killed on the day of Badr. And the answer of لَوْلَا is indicated by what precedes it.
